Hello everyone!👋

Oi-Tersken Innovative School, nestled in high mountains where stars seem close enough to touch and our ancestors navigated by them. Combining curiosity about the universe with modern knowledge, we develop innovative thinking.
We are young researchers passionate about science, technology, and space. Our goal is to build a creative project using NASA data to unlock space's most fascinating mysteries.
summary:
Project Name
1. SPACE ANALOG — an interactive digital platform developed to explore unique geographical regions on Earth and compare their natural conditions with those of the Moon and Mars.
High-Level Project Summary
SPACE ANALOG is an interactive digital application designed to explore different regions of the world, view their climatic and geographical indicators, and compare them with one another. The application compares the characteristics of terrestrial regions with scientific data from the Moon and Mars, allowing for the conditional modeling of a space habitat base.
The project combines global-scale comparison with local research. The application retains the ability to view regions across various countries and natural zones around the world. At the same time, the Ak-Sai Valley, Köl-Suu, and Köl-Tör in the Naryn Region of Kyrgyzstan are examined in depth as special research case studies of the project.
This approach helps students compare not just a single region, but deserts, high mountains, icy areas, and arid landscapes across different continents, enabling them to understand which indicators are similar and which differ drastically.
Using open NASA data, the platform is aimed at exploring climatic and geographical indicators, comparing regions, and modeling a conditional space habitat base. The project increases students' interest in astronomy, physics, geography, ecology, and modern technologies.
details:
Project Details

A structured scientific database was created featuring 17 unique Earth analogue locations similar to the Moon and Mars, along with high-altitude research sites in Kyrgyzstan (Naryn, Ak-Sai, Kel-Suu, Son-Kol, Chatyr-Kol, and Kol-Tor).

Software and Hosting. The web application is deployed and hosted online via the Netlify cloud platform. • Tools and APIs. OpenStreetMap and the Leaflet.js interactive mapping library, official scientific datasets from NASA, USGS, and Ramsar, as well as AI assistance for structuring data and optimizing code. Workflow. Our "SPACE ANALOG" platform allows users to explore, analyze, and compare planetary analogues on Earth for space research. Users can filter locations in the catalog by target planetary body (Moon or Mars) and geological type, and view their exact coordinates on an interactive global map. Additionally, the platform includes a dedicated Compare Tool. Researchers and students can select between 2 and 5 locations simultaneously to compare their temperature, atmospheric pressure, and terrain side-by-side. A key highlight of the project is scientifically showcasing the high-altitude regions of Kyrgyzstan as promising analog testbeds for future space exploration.

Creativity. We developed a creative interface that balances scientific accuracy with visual simplicity. Instead of arbitrary scores or overly complex numbers, we used clear comparison tables, interactive map markers, and documented scientific facts. Our goal is to make space exploration and the scientific potential of Kyrgyzstan's landscapes engaging, accessible, and intuitive for everyone. Attention (Key Focus). Our design prioritizes user-friendliness with a clean and effective interface (UI) that presents scientific data accurately. By utilizing official datasets from NASA, USGS, and Ramsar, SPACE ANALOG covers lunar and Martian analogue sites worldwide alongside the high-altitude regions of Kyrgyzstan. This approach ensures data reliability and enables researchers and students to easily explore and compare planetary environments. Impact The SPACE ANALOG project bridges science and education, delivering meaningful benefits to students, researchers, and the broader community: • Accessible Space Education. Students and young learners can easily grasp complex planetary environments through interactive maps and visual sideby-side comparisons without overwhelming technical jargon. • Highlighting Kyrgyzstan’s Scientific Potential. The platform showcases high-altitude regions in Naryn (Ak-Sai, Kel-Suu, Son-Kol, Chatyr-Kol, and Kol-Tor) as promising international testbeds for planetary analogue research. • Promoting Scientific Accuracy. By presenting both terrestrial similarities and critical planetary differences (such as gravity, atmosphere, and radiation), the project encourages evidence-based critical thinking.

Future Plans We plan to expand SPACE ANALOG into a comprehensive scientific and educational ecosystem through the following steps: • 3D Panoramas and Virtual Tours. Integrating 360-degree virtual field trips so users can explore locations like the Ak-Sai Valley or the Atacama Desert remotely. • Expanding the Global Catalog. Adding more extreme environments across Central Asia and worldwide, including volcanic fields, salt flats, and permafrost zones. • Mobile App and Offline Access. Developing a dedicated mobile version with offline map and data support for field researchers working in remote areas without internet connectivity. Educational Partnerships. Collaborating with schools and universities to integrate the platform as an interactive learning tool for astronomy and geography classes.
